description: Conformance corpus for scripts that exhaust the stack. Plain recursion, recursion through the engine's own built-ins, and recursion over deeply nested data must each end with an error the script can catch, or simply succeed; none may take down the engine, the host process, or a later call. A runtime whose engine recurses on a native stack it does not measure must bound that recursion itself.
notes: Each case's `script` is spliced into `template` at `SCRIPT`, and the runtime executes the result. It must evaluate to `"caught"` (the recursion stopped with an error the script caught) or `"ok"` (the runtime carried it to the end). Which of the two is the runtime's own business: a corpus case never requires a deep recursion to succeed, because engines bound different built-ins at different depths.
After every case the same runtime executes `after`, which must evaluate to `afterExpected`: an exhausted stack leaves the runtime usable. Disposing the runtime afterwards must not fail.
A deep value is built with a loop, and deep JSON text with `Array.prototype.join`, so building it never recurses; only the operation the case names does.

The manifest's `timeout_ms` is generous on purpose. Building and walking 100000 levels is slow on some engines and on small machines, and a case is about the stack, not the time budget, so running out of time would only hide what the case checks.
after: (function () { function depth(n) { return n === 0 ? 0 : 1 + depth(n - 1); } return depth(100) + JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({ a: [1, 2] })).a.length; })()

cases.name: recursion carrying arguments and locals
cases.script: function f(n, a, b) { var c = [n, a, b]; return f(n + 1, c, { n: n }) + 1; } f(0, null, null);

cases.name: mutual recursion
cases.script: function a(n) { return b(n + 1) + 1; } function b(n) { return a(n + 1) + 1; } a(0);

cases.name: recursion through a getter
cases.script: var o = { get x() { return o.x; } }; o.x;

cases.name: recursion through toString
cases.script: var o = {}; o.toString = function () { return String(o); }; String(o);

cases.name: recursion through toJSON
cases.script: var o = { toJSON: function () { return JSON.stringify(o); } }; JSON.stringify(o);

cases.name: recursive descent over a deeply nested object
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = { d: v }; function walk(o) { return typeof o === 'object' ? walk(o.d) + 1 : 0; } walk(v);

cases.name: JSON.stringify of a deeply nested object
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = { d: v }; JSON.stringify(v);

cases.name: JSON.stringify of a deeply nested array
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = [v]; JSON.stringify(v);

cases.name: JSON.stringify of a deeply nested value with a replacer
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = { d: v }; JSON.stringify(v, function (k, x) { return x; });

cases.name: JSON.stringify of a deeply nested value with a property list
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = { d: v, e: 1 }; JSON.stringify(v, ['d']);

cases.name: String of a deeply nested array
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = [v]; String(v);

cases.name: flattening a deeply nested array
cases.script: var v = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = [v]; v.flat(Infinity);

cases.name: a long chain of proxies
cases.script: var p = {}; for (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) p = new Proxy(p, {}); p.x;

cases.name: a long chain of bound functions
cases.script: var f = function () { return 1; }; for (var i = 0; i < 10000; i++) f = f.bind(null); f();
